Subject: Mix of Q3 production programs and supporting initiatives to maximize contribution

Hi team,

We’re preparing the Q3 plan for our distillery and ready-to-drink portfolio. The objective is to maximize total margin while respecting the plant’s operating capacities, storage, quality, shipping, environmental limits, inventory, and our variable operating budget. Below are the levers we can pull this quarter, with how each one contributes value and uses or frees our constrained resources. Each item can be scheduled from zero up to the maximum noted.

- Heritage Rye batches (up to 15.76 runs; 4.5 contribution points per run). Each run occupies 6.49 fermentation tank-days and 4.94 bottling line hours, while freeing 4.07 units of cold storage capacity because the batch bypasses our internal chill staging.

- Bourbon mash expansion (up to 11.75 runs; 5.25 contribution points per run). Each run requires 3.53 mash house hours and taps 3.38 units from the variable operating budget.

- Botanical gin special (up to 7.53 runs; 6.78 contribution points per run). Each run draws 6.55 mash house hours, 6.67 bottling line hours, 4.56 quality lab hours, 4.69 units from our CO2 utilization quota, and 9.9 units of glass bottle inventory. The program brings 3.12 units of budget relief per run via partner funding and reduces our emissions/discharge pressure by 0.92 cap units per run thanks to the cleaner distillation cycle.

- Operations efficiency sprints (up to 9.3 sprints; 1.06 contribution points per sprint). Each sprint frees 3.29 mash house hours, 2.97 shipping dock slots, and 4.89 emissions/discharge cap units by tightening setups, consolidating loads, and improving thermal recovery.

- RTD cocktail launch (up to 8.18 runs; 1.8 contribution points per run). Each run requires 7.0 units of distillation column throughput, 2.12 bottling line hours, 2.05 units of cold storage, 5.3 shipping dock slots, and 9.55 units of glass bottle inventory, and uses 4.56 emissions/discharge cap units.

- Seasonal hard seltzer (up to 10.97 runs; 5.0 contribution points per run). Each run uses 2.62 fermentation tank-days and 2.24 units from our CO2 utilization quota, while freeing 0.89 bottling line hours and 0.58 cold storage units due to faster turns and ambient staging. It requires 4.89 shipping dock slots per run.

- Heat-recovery retrofit packages (up to 17.9 packages; 3.75 contribution points per package). Each package consumes 7.06 mash house hours during installation and tuning, and then frees 1.21 fermentation tank-days, 1.42 bottling line hours, 1.16 cold storage units, 0.53 units of our CO2 utilization quota, and 0.13 units of glass bottle inventory by reducing hold times and changeover waste.

- Single malt expansion (up to 14.0 runs; 5.97 contribution points per run). Each run requires 0.37 mash house hours, 6.27 units of distillation column throughput, 6.33 fermentation tank-days, 7.66 bottling line hours, and 9.86 budget units.

- Small-batch brandy program (up to 6.45 runs; 7.5 contribution points per run). Each run frees 3.49 fermentation tank-days by using excess capacity at our partner’s facility, while drawing 7.78 bottling line hours and 1.68 budget units.

- Wholesale club packs (up to 19.94 runs; 5.2 contribution points per run). Each run brings 1.36 mash house hours back to the schedule through simplified processing, and consumes 3.27 budget units, 2.17 quality lab hours, and 6.11 shipping dock slots.

- Premium barrel‑aged release (up to 17.51 runs; 8.61 contribution points per run). Each run requires 7.19 cold storage units for maturation and staging, 2.68 units of glass bottle inventory, and 2.91 emissions/discharge cap units. The campaign is largely distributor‑funded, freeing 3.14 budget units per run, and uses outsourced drop shipping that frees 3.36 shipping dock slots per run.

- Store‑brand co‑pack (up to 15.11 runs; 5.98 contribution points per run). Each run frees 2.21 mash house hours and 0.19 units of distillation column throughput by reusing client‑supplied base spirits, while requiring 3.88 cold storage units, 3.72 shipping dock slots, and 2.38 units of our CO2 utilization quota. It also frees 3.38 units of glass bottle inventory because the customer supplies packaging.

- Reserve bourbon (up to 9.77 runs; 8.87 contribution points per run). Each run requires 6.88 units of distillation column throughput, 9.75 fermentation tank-days, 3.44 budget units, 3.62 units of glass bottle inventory, and 3.91 emissions/discharge cap units.
